kurz: When curing, salt preserves the meat. Nitrite in curing salt also keeps it pink and protects against dangerous germs.
bild_im_kopf: Like a museum conservator: they keep the painting fresh and the colours bright, but they change how it looks.
was_passiert: Salt draws out water and slows down germs. Curing salt also contains a little nitrite. It binds to the red muscle pigment, which then stays pink even when cooked: that is why ham is pink but a roast is grey. Nitrite also inhibits dangerous bacteria and gives the typical ham flavour.
warum_wichtig: Explains why ham and frankfurters are pink but roasts are not, and why curing salt is not used like table salt.
faustregeln: Dose curing salt only as the recipe says; do not use it in place of table salt.
Do not sear or grill cured meat hard; at very high heat unwanted substances can form.
Pink colour in cured meat does not mean raw.

praxis.text: Cooked ham is cured and cooked, which is why it is pink. An uncured pork roast turns grey at the same temperature.
